title: endpoint-fastpath-ux-scenarios-and-copy-lab
body:
Purpose: quick exploration of a condensed endpoint creation flow ("fastpath") that surfaces model-catalog cards, lightweight pinning controls, and deterministic fallback copy. This doc captures wireframe notes, microcopy variants, scenario-driven acceptance criteria, and grooming items for the backlog.

High-level goals:
- Fast path: let an engineer create an HTTP endpoint in <= 3 clicks for common cases (single model, default runtime).
- Make model pinning explicit but low-friction: default is 'auto route' with an optional 'pin version' toggle that preserves expected semantics.
- Surface fallbacks and cost/latency tradeoffs clearly when choosing variants.
- Provide copy that reduces ambiguity about what pinning means for rollouts, cache invalidation, and billing.

Wireframe fragments (compact card layout):
- Catalog list: compact horizontal cards with small model badge, version dropdown chevron (default hidden), latency/cost micro-metrics inline (e.g., "p99 80ms · 0.9¢/k tok"). Card click selects model and opens the fastpath drawer.
- Fastpath drawer: three rows: Target name (auto-suggested from model), Runtime & capacity (defaults: standard GPU, autoscale on), Pinning row (radio: Auto route | Pin to version).
- Pining control micro-interaction: when user chooses "Pin to version" a compact inline list shows the top 3 candidate versions with short notes (e.g., "v2.1 — 7% fewer hallucinations on our evals"). Small info icon opens a tooltip with link "What does pinning do?"
- Fallback policy selector (small text under pin row): Dropdown: "No fallback / Fallback to auto-route / Fallback to pinned-alternative". Tooltip explains impact on availability and cost.

Microcopy candidates (goal: precise, short, non-technical where possible):
- Fastpath header: "Create endpoint — quick" (alt: "Quick endpoint")
- Model card metric: "p99 80ms · 0.9¢/k tok" (tooltip: "Measured on standard test trace; your workload may vary")
- Pin toggle label: "Pin version (stable outputs)"
- Pin tooltip body: "Pinning locks this endpoint to a specific model version. Useful for preventing unexpected quality regressions during rollouts. Pinned endpoints will not automatically receive version updates, and may affect availability during scale events."
- Auto route label: "Auto route (managed updates)"
- Fallback policy short copy: "Fallback: keep serving if pinned version is unavailable" (alt: "Fallback to compatible model" )
- Confirm CTA: "Create endpoint" (secondary action: "Create & test")

Edge cases & UX decisions:
- If a pinned version is retired by model owners, show inline banner: "Pinned version vX.Y is retired — choose a replacement or switch to Auto route." CTA: "Pick replacement" / "Switch to Auto route". Banner persists until resolved.
- If user pins a bleeding-edge experimental version, surface a small risk tag: "experimental — expect behavioral drift" with link to model-release notes.
- When pinning increases expected cost by >30% (based on runtime/capacity delta) show an inline cost hint: "Estimated +32% cost per token" (requires cheap cost estimator service).
- Accessibility: ensure all toggles, radio groups, and dropdowns are keyboard-focusable, with ARIA labels that include the selected pin status and fallback policy.

Acceptance criteria (fastpath MVP):
- User can open fastpath from a selected model card and create an endpoint with default settings in <= 3 clicks.
- Pinning control is present and persists in endpoint metadata (visible in endpoint settings page).
- Fallback policy saves and is honored by routing (server-side) — here we verify via integration test triggered by PROD-2113.
- Microcopy for pin tooltip, fallback, and retired-version banner approved by legal/comms (link in linked_artifacts).

Grooming backlog (tasks & rough estimates):
- UX: high-fidelity wires for compact cards and drawer (3d) — owner: Riley — jira:PROD-2150.
- Frontend: implement compact catalog card, fastpath drawer shell, pin control (5d) — owner: Diego — jira:PROD-2151.
- Backend: endpoint create API supports pin meta + fallback enum (3d) — owner: Platform — jira:PROD-2152.
- E2E: test pinning and fallback behavior under degraded cluster simulation (4d) — owner: SRE — jira:PROD-2153.
- Docs: add page to "How pinning works" and quickstart snippet (1d) — owner: Docs — jira:PROD-2154.

Open questions for review (decision needed in next sync):
- Default: should fastpath default to "Pin to latest stable" or "Auto route"? My recommendation: default to Auto route and expose a clear badge when users choose Pin. Rationale: reduces surprise/upkeep burden for new users.
- What is the canonical definition of "stable" across catalog models? Need research input from Applied ML on version tagging.
- Should cost impact be shown pre-submit for orgs with reserved capacity? (If yes, need integration with Dedicated billing estimator.)

Quick copy experiments to A/B test (metrics = click-through to advanced create flow, successful create without changing defaults):
- Variant A: CTA "Create endpoint" / Pin label "Pin version (stable outputs)"
- Variant B: CTA "Create endpoint" / Pin label "Lock to version (prevent updates)"
- Variant C: CTA "Create & test" primary, "Create" secondary (test vs single CTA)

Next steps / meeting agenda (triage in product sync 2025-03-04):
- Present wires + microcopy, finalize default pin behavior (Asha).
- Confirm backend schema for endpoint.metadata.pin and fallback enum (Platform lead).
- Prioritize PROD-2151/2152 for Q2 sprint planning.

Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally compact: the goal is to unblock engineering for a fast MVP that reduces friction for internal demos and customer POCs. I expect follow-ups to expand the advanced create flow (route policies, workspace scoping, advanced capacity tuning).

Raw sketch references (quick):
- Sketch A: compact card w/ chevron -> drawer (hand-drawn) — see attached slide in PR-408.
- Sketch B: inline pin list micro-interaction — prototype notes in Confluence PC-5242.

Owner contact: Asha.Kapoor@redwood.ai
